question: When share is issued at a price equal to its face value, it is called issue
explanation: A share is issued at par when the issue price equals the face (nominal) value. No securities premium or discount arises in this case.

why_not.B: Premium means issue price is more than face value.
why_not.C: Discount means issue price is less than face value.
why_not.D: Bonus issue is free allotment to members out of reserves, not a price comparison.

exam_tip: Par = equal, premium = above, discount = below face value.
